recs.x:
a thin layer of integration tests (Selenium/Capybara/Whatever), which drive out unit tests for the individual components. If you let the tests drive your code design, and follow the "Red -> Green -> Refactor" workflow, it tends to shepherd you into writing small easily testable functions and objects that are loosely coupled.

You can also use TDD to salvage crappy code, and derive good design even after the damage has been done. For a beautiful demonstration of this process at work, I strongly recommend Katrina Owen's video on "Therapeutic Refactoring". [link]
